content:
With Lionfish's Phase 1 kernel driver interception, interactive “Press to Identify” raw input mode, and device naming established, the next phase pivots the desktop interface toward the modern Windows 11 Fluent Design System.

Planned updates upon resumption:

  • Fluent Design System Alignment: Elevate the desktop experience to native Windows 11 Fluent standards with layered surfaces, subtle 1px elevation borders, refined 6px–8px corner radii, and Segoe UI Variable typography (with seamless Segoe UI fallback for Windows 10).
  • Light / Dark / System Theme Switching: Implement a 3-way theme mode in Settings (System, Light, Dark) with a live Windows registry listener (AppsUseLightTheme) for real-time theme adaptation without restarts. The brand #FF6B35 Lionfish orange accent will remain active across all modes.
  • Light Gray Device Cards: Replace the initial dark blue device card backgrounds with crisp light gray / elevated neutral surfaces in Light mode (and neutral slate gray in Dark mode), featuring subtle borders and gentle orange identification flashes.
  • Master Keyboard Pinned to Top: Ensure the protected Master Keyboard is always pinned to the top of the device list (index 0), followed by configured macro pads and unassigned devices, automatically reordering whenever roles change.
  • Key Map & Macro Automation Pipeline: Continue wiring intercepted scan codes directly to action dispatch and macro playback.

Pausing for the night with clean builds and all design specs documented in the implementation plan.
title: Lionfish Fluent Design System pivot, Light/Dark/System themes, and Master Keyboard pinning roadmap
